correctness.rationale: For WQ≠0 the W derivative is nonzero. At WQ=0 off the vertex the spatial gradient on the surface is −∇P, so over each triple p the singular locus is [0:p] when Q(p)≠0 and an entire line when Q(p)=0. In the avoiding case there is no common branch component, and the valuation of P/Q³ at a branch line is 1, proving generic cubic irreducibility; primitivity gives integrality. The isolated singularities then give R1 and the hypersurface gives S2. The cubic cone over each triple has smooth plane cubic section, with μ=8 and p_g=1. For c=e(C), t=#(B∩C), and e(B)=−6, projection from the vertex gives three-sheeted étale, singleton, empty, and affine-line strata. With compactly supported Euler additivity and the vertex included this gives 22−3c+3t. A smooth nonic has e=459, and the isolated Milnor Euler jumps in complex dimension two give μ_v=459−e(S_Q)−96. The degree-six lowest term gives multiplicity six. The common function field is the cyclic cover T³=P and has the cited abelian birational type, so a smooth projective resolution has χ(O)=0. The discrepancy with hypersurface χ(O)=57 is the sum of the thirteen local geometric genera; removing the twelve unit contributions gives 45. Exact intersections for the three quadratic ranks yield all the stated conditional formulas: (c,t)=(2,18−r), (3,18) or (3,17), and (2,9). The formula is only for normal parameters, and does not assert an analytic type or that every possible tangent count occurs. Independent finite replay: `python /workspace/branches/independent_math.py hesse` used exact Q(ζ₃) arithmetic, dual conic tests and kernel tests for five illustrative normal cases; this checks the input strata and their computed values, not Milnor numbers independently of the proof.

value.rationale: The result identifies which special degree-nine models of the same abelian birational type stay normal, and computes the isolated vertex invariant on those boundaries without mistaking birational equivalence for equivalence of singularities. The tangent and nonreduced cases change the Milnor number even though the common function field does not change. This parameter sensitivity, not the already covered transverse value, is the useful contribution.
